physics_goals.quote: CERES pioneered the measurement of electron-positron pairs at the SPS.
physics_goals.value: Measure electron-positron pairs in heavy-ion collisions as a probe of thermal radiation, deconfinement and chiral symmetry restoration

summary.plain: CERES (NA45) was a CERN experiment that detected pairs of electrons and positrons from heavy-ion collisions, a clean probe of the hot, dense matter. It found more low-mass electron pairs than hadron decays can explain, from sulphur-gold to lead-gold collisions, 1992 to 2000.
summary.technical: CERES/NA45: electron-pair spectrometer with two Ring Imaging Cherenkov detectors in a field-free region and silicon drift tracking (upgraded with a radial-drift TPC), measuring low-mass e+e- in S-Au (1992), p-A (1993) and Pb-Au (1995, 1996, 1999, 2000) collisions: enhancement of low-mass pairs and a strong in-medium broadening of the rho.
